output:
In front of my bed shines bright moonlight,
Misinterpreting it as frost on ground.
Looking up at the clear sky's glow,
My heart turns to thoughts of home dear.

Red beans grow in southern lands,
Spring brings forth many branches anew.
May you gather them abundantly,
For this is the thing most dear to me.

In front of my bed shines the moonlight,
Thought it was frost on the ground below.
I raise my head to gaze at the clear sky,
Then lower mine eyes toward home.

Often remember the day when I visited the stream at sunset,
drunk and unaware of my return route.
When all was over with the fun,
I returned in the evening on my boat.
I hurriedly tried to find its way out,
only to be startled by a flock of geese flying about.
Scrambling back and forth,
I couldn't find my way out.

Note: The original text contains some ambiguity due to the use of "争渡" which can mean both "scramble" or "to struggle". In this context, it is translated as "hurriedly try to find its way out" for clarity.

Red beans grow in southern lands,
Spring brings forth how many branches?
May you take much from this,
For it holds the most longing hearts.

Often I recall my day in the stream,
drunk and unaware of returning paths.
In high spirits, I return home late on boat,
and accidentally enter deep amidst lotus flowers.
I struggle to cross over,
struggle to cross over,
awakening startled by a flock of egrets and storks.

Often remember the day when sunset bathed the willow bank,
Lost in pleasure I did not realize my return path.
Exhausted from the boat's journey at dusk,
I turned back to explore the deep lotus pond.
Scrambling through the shallows, seeking to leave,
The startled egrets and ducks took flight on every wave.

Beside my bed, bright moonlight gleams,
Misguidedly, I think it's frost on ground.
Peering up, at clear skies above,
Gazing down, I miss my hometown.

Moonlight on the bed,
Thought it was frost below.
Looking up at the bright moon,
Bowing my head for home.

Moonlight on the bed,
Misbelieving it's frosty ground.
Looking up at the clear moon,
Lowering my gaze to think of home.

Red beans grow in southern lands,
Spring brings forth how many branches?
May you gather them often,
This is the thing most treasured.

I live at the head of the Yangtze River,
You live at its tail.
Every day I think of you but cannot see you,
We drink the same river water together.
This water will never dry up,
This sorrow will not cease.
May your heart be like mine,
And my love for you shall never disappoint.

I live at the head of the Yangtze,
You dwell at its tail.
Every day I think of you but cannot see you,
We drink the same river water together.
This water will never stop flowing,
This sorrow will never cease.
Only hope that your heart is as true as mine,
I will not let my love go unfulfilled.

I live at the head of the Yangtze,
You dwell at its tail.
Every day I think of you but cannot see you;
We drink the same river's water together.
This water will never dry up,
This sorrow will never cease.
I hope your heart is like mine too,
I do not want to let you down.

Always remember the sun-drenched evening at the stream,
Drunk beyond returning home,
In pursuit of pleasure until dusk sets,
I mistakenly found my way to the depths of lotus flowers.

Scrambling back and forth,
Awakening a flock of egrets and storks on the shore.

I live at the head of the Yangtze,
You reside at its tail.
Every day I think of you but see no sign of you,
We drink from the same river.
This water will never cease to flow,
This sorrow will never end.
May your heart be true to mine,
And my love for you shall never fail.

Here is the English translation of the poem:

Red Beans Born in Southern Lands
Spring Comes and They Grow Many Branches
May You Take Much From This, And Remember Me

This poem expresses deep longing and affection for someone who has been missed or forgotten. The "red beans" symbolize the poet's love and desire to be remembered by the recipient. The line "may you take much from this" suggests that the poet hopes the recipient will remember them fondly and appreciate their presence in their life. Overall, it conveys a sense of yearning and attachment between two people separated by time.

Every day I think about you but cannot see you
We drink from the same river and share the same water
This water has never stopped flowing
And this sorrow will never end
I only hope that your heart is like mine
And I promise to fulfill my love for you.

Drunk and unaware of my return path.
Endless joy led back the boat late at night,
Entering deep within the lotus pond's secluded shore.
Crossing, crossing again,
Awakening a flock of egrets on the tranquil ripples.

I promise to fulfill my love for you.

In front of my bed shines the moonlight,
As if it were frost on the ground.
I raise my head to gaze at the bright moon,
And lower mine eyes to miss home.

Remembering the sun-dappled evening by the stream,
Lost in wine until I forgot my way back home.
At dusk, I returned on my boat,
Only to find myself deep within the lotus pond's embrace.
Crossing again and again,
I startled a flock of egrets as they flew away.

I live at the head of the Yangtze,

We drink the same river water together.

This sorrow will never be resolved.
May your heart truly love me as my heart loves you,
I promise to fulfill your deep longing.

I live at the head of the Yangtze,
You reside at its tail.
Every day I think of you but see no sign of you,
We drink the same river water together.
This water has been flowing for ages,
How long will this sorrow last?
Only hope that your heart is as pure as mine,
And I won't let my love go unfulfilled.

Often remember the sun-drenched evening by the stream,
Drunk beyond returning home,
In deep dusk, I paddled back late,
Strayed into the depths of lotus pond.

Crossing again and again,
Trembling at startling birds flying.

Moonlight on the bed,
Thought it was frost on earth.
Looking up at the bright moon,
Bowing my head for home.

Moonlight shining on the bed,
I doubt it's frost on the ground.
Looking up at the bright moon,
My thoughts drift to my hometown.

Red beans grow in southern lands,
Spring brings forth how many branches?
May you take much from this,
This is the most treasured thing.

Red beans grow in southern lands,
Springtime brings forth how many branches?
May you take much of this for your own;
This thing is most dear to me.
